== Biography ==

The Cheshire Cat is a creature of Wonderland known for its fixed and perpetual grin. It possesses very long claws and a great many teeth, features that lend it a formidable aspect; yet its good-natured appearance convinced Alice that it warranted respectful treatment. The Cat possesses the remarkable ability to vanish and reappear at will, sometimes materializing as only a grin suspended in the air before the rest of its form becomes visible.

The Cat is conversable and inclined toward philosophical observation. When Alice asked which way she ought to go, it replied: "That depends a good deal on where you want to get to." Alice found its company agreeable and regarded it as a friend in Wonderland, even securing it under her arm to prevent its escape. The Cat seemed equally content with her presence and spoke readily in reply.

The Cat's appearance at court occasioned considerable commotion. A dispute broke out among the executioner, the King, and the Queen, with all three arguing whilst others stood by in discomfort. The King regarded it with suspicion, declaring he did not like the look of it at all, though he permitted the creature to kiss his hand if it wished. Thus the Cheshire Cat, despite its amiable nature, seemed to stir unease among Wonderland's formal inhabitants.

== Narrative role ==

The Cheshire Cat first appears to Alice sitting on a tree bough. When it sees her, the Cat grins. According to Alice, the Cat appears good-natured, though its very long claws and many teeth indicate it should be treated with respect. When Alice asks which way she ought to go, the Cat replies that it depends a good deal on where one wants to get to.

The Cheshire Cat possesses a peculiar ability: it can vanish and reappear. When Alice encounters it again later, she first perceives only a grin in the air, puzzling over the appearance until she recognizes it as the Cat. She is pleased to have someone to talk to. The Cat asks her "How are you getting on?" As it speaks, more of its form materializes.

Alice introduces the Cat to the King, calling it "a friend of mine—a Cheshire Cat." The King regards it with curiosity but does not like its appearance. He does offer, however, to let it kiss his hand if it wishes.

A large crowd gathers around the Cheshire Cat. A dispute erupts among the executioner, the King, and the Queen, all speaking at once while the rest of the crowd remains silent and uncomfortable. During this contention, the Cat's head disappears, and the three continue arguing about whether a creature can be beheaded when only its head remains.

== Personality ==

The Cheshire Cat is known above all for its perpetual grin and affable nature. When Alice first encountered it perched upon a tree bough, it greeted her with nothing more than that characteristic grin, and to her eyes it appeared good-natured enough. Yet this gentle demeanor coexists with undeniable physical presence: the creature possessed very long claws and a great many teeth, qualities that inspired both wariness and respect in those who observed it.

The Cat proves conversant and reflective, engaging Alice in philosophical discourse without hesitation. When asked which way she ought to go, it responds with considered observation: "That depends a good deal on where you want to get to." This readiness to converse suggests a creature of wit, capable of genuine companionship rather than mere animal reaction.

There remains something strangely ethereal about the Cheshire Cat's very nature. It manifests in the most unusual manner—appearing first as nothing but a disembodied grin suspended in the air, only gradually becoming whole as mouth and form coalesce into visibility. This partial and dreamlike appearance lends the creature an enigmatic quality, as though it exists at the threshold between solid presence and phantasm. Yet despite its strangeness, the Cat becomes a source of comfort to Alice, who counts it as a true friend amidst the bewildering events of Wonderland.

== Appearance ==

The Cheshire Cat is a creature of striking peculiarity. It possesses very long claws and a great many teeth, characteristics that, despite its good-natured appearance, command respect. The creature is remembered chiefly for its grin—a feature so distinctive that Alice first recognized it by this expression alone, identifying the spreading smile in the air before she could discern the rest of the creature. It is small enough to be tucked comfortably under one's arm and can perch upon the boughs of trees.

== Powers ==

The Cheshire Cat possesses the extraordinary ability to vanish and materialize in parts. Rather than disappearing entirely at once, it can fade away piecemeal, with certain features persisting or materializing independently—most notably, its grin. When Alice first spotted the creature in the air, only its grin was visible to her. When it spoke, it did so "as soon as there was mouth enough for it to speak with," indicating the mouth materialized before the rest of the form. This peculiar faculty for fragmented existence distinguishes the Cheshire Cat among Wonderland's inhabitants.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Alice]]''' — acquaintance. Alice regards the Cheshire Cat as a friend and seeks its company for conversation and guidance, introducing it to others with familiar affection.

'''[[King]]''' — enemy. The King seems to regard the Cat with disfavor, stating that he does not like the look of it, though he offers it a stiffly courteous gesture.

'''[[Queen]]''' — enemy. The Queen becomes embroiled in a dispute concerning the Cat, alongside the King and the executioner, suggesting some conflict or concern regarding its presence.

== Trivia ==

* The Cheshire Cat's grin is so distinctive that Alice recognizes it by the smile alone, appearing mysteriously in the air before the rest of the creature becomes visible.
* The Cat's form materializes gradually, with the grin appearing first and the mouth growing large enough for it to speak.
* Upon first observing the Cat, the King expressed displeasure at its appearance, though he offered permission for it to kiss his hand.
* The Cheshire Cat drew the attention of Wonderland's authorities—the King, Queen, and Executioner all engaged in dispute over its fate, which gathered quite a large crowd of onlookers.
